meta.title: AI Process Integration ROI Library
meta.evidence_bar: A case enters only if a named company (or a rigorous study) states a quantified before/after outcome for a specific business process. Anonymous claims and vendor aggregates without a named customer are excluded.

confidence_tiers.High: Peer-reviewed or randomized field study, or a company figure reproduced consistently over time
confidence_tiers.Medium-high: Named company, named executive, stated baseline and timeframe; vendor may host the story
confidence_tiers.Medium: Named company and metric but missing baseline or timeframe; self-reported

summary: Roughly 88% of large organizations use AI somewhere, yet only 37% attribute any EBIT impact to it and about 6% attribute 5% or more (McKinsey, Aug 2026).

The companies that capture value pick a narrow, high-volume process with a clean baseline, redesign the workflow (73% of high performers vs 25% of others), and measure against the pre-AI baseline for at least a quarter.
Back-office finance and operations produce the most reliable quantified returns; budgets skew to sales and marketing despite better ROI in operations and finance (MIT NANDA).
Headcount headlines have a poor track record: Klarna, Commonwealth Bank and Duolingo each walked back or reframed AI-for-people announcements within a year.
Buy or embed for the first wave (vendor tools succeed about twice as often as internal builds), expect 3-12 month payback on good cases and nothing on pilots without a baseline.

benchmarks.metric: AR: share of AI users reducing DSO

macro.adoption: ~9 in 10 use AI in at least one function; 44% scaling enterprise-wide
macro.return: 37% attribute any EBIT impact (flat vs 2025); 6% high performers (5%+ of EBIT)
macro.finding: 40% of $1B+ firms scaling agents (up from 27%); 73% of high performers redesigned workflows vs 25%; 20% constrained by AI operating costs

macro.adoption: 88% of organizations use AI (78% in 2024); 79% use gen AI
macro.return: Cost decreases most cited in software engineering and manufacturing (56%); revenue gains most cited in marketing and sales (67%)
macro.finding: Global corporate AI investment $581.7B in 2025, up ~130%; most reported gains under 10% cost or 5% revenue

macro.return: 5% future-built, 35% scalers, 60% laggards with minimal gains
macro.finding: Leaders 1.7x revenue growth, 1.6x EBIT margin, 3.6x 3-yr TSR; 70% of AI value in core functions, IT only 13%

macro.study: BCG Building business value with AI investment
macro.adoption: Leaders invest 1.7% of revenue in AI vs 0.8%
macro.return: Leaders report 3x cost reduction and 2.7x ROIC
macro.finding: 10-20-70 rule: 10% algorithms, 20% technology and data, 70% people, process and behavior change

macro.adoption: 90% of workers use personal AI tools daily; 40% of firms have official subscriptions
macro.return: 95% see no measurable return; ~5% of integrated pilots extract millions in value
macro.finding: Vendor-built tools succeed about twice as often as internal builds; $2-10M/yr documented replacing outsourced support and document review

macro.study: Deloitte State of AI in the Enterprise
macro.adoption: 60% of workers have sanctioned AI tools (under 40% prior year)
macro.return: Only 25% have moved 40%+ of pilots into production
macro.finding: 30% redesigning key processes; 37% surface-level use; 21% have mature agent governance

macro.adoption: 59% of finance functions use AI; AP automation 37%, anomaly detection 34%
macro.return: 91% report low or moderate impact initially
macro.finding: Finance adoption steady rather than accelerating
40%+ of agentic AI projects canceled by end-2027; only ~130 of thousands of agent vendors are real

macro.sample: Biweekly national survey of employer firms
macro.adoption: 17-20% of all firms; 37% of firms with 250+ employees; 39.7% Information, 33.9% Finance and Insurance, ~14% Retail
macro.finding: Adoption rising only among firms with 20+ employees; Fed (Apr 2026) puts worker-level gen AI use at ~41%

macro.adoption: Chatbots widespread; most employers encourage use
macro.return: Average time savings 2.8%; no significant effect on earnings or hours
macro.finding: Individual chatbot use without process change yields small, unmonetized gains
